episodes.199420: Thunderstorms developed north of a warm front during the evening hours on Friday (3/28).  The strongest storms produced hail up to half dollar size across central Wisconsin.
episodes.199715: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon over southeast Minnesota and west-central Wisconsin, producing a few instances of marginally severe and sub-severe hail. ||An isolated cell blossomed quickly along a boundary over south-central Minnesota, resulting in a strong downward gust as it weakened.
episodes.200625: A dryline and cold front moved through North and Central Texas, with storms developing along and ahead of the boundaries. Some storms were able to become severe with large hail and damaging winds the main threats. The largest hail stone was 2 inches and fell in Comanche County. Additionally, the highest wind gust was 61 MPH which occurred at the McKinney ASOS.
episodes.200752: A line of thunderstorms moved through the Bay of Green Bay late on the 28th, causing strong thunderstorm wind gusts at Minneapolis Shoal.
episodes.200812: A rapid increase in tropical moisture depth transporting northward along the southwest flank of a large lower tropospheric Northwestern Atlantic Ridge resulted a training convective cells across the Lower Florida Keys from Key West through Sugarloaf Key.  Gale-force wind gusts occurred as the result of thunderstorm outflows projecting northwest across the coastal waters.
episodes.200940: Two rounds of storms developed throughout the day on March 28th and produced large hail across southeast Minnesota. The first of these occurred early in the morning when a storm moved through portions of Fillmore and Houston counties, producing up to ping pong ball sized hail. Later that day during the afternoon and evening, additional storms developed and produced hail up to half dollar sized.
episodes.200989: A series of upper disturbances and a slow moving cold front created multiple days of stormy weather across portions of Louisiana. Severe weather and flooding occurred.
episodes.201166: An upper level system moved across the area very slowly on March 29th. The flow pattern in the upper levels were quite conducive for sustained thunderstorm growth. Add in ample moisture in place to produce moderate to heavy rain and the environment was prime for producing flash flooding. Training thunderstorms in the Baton Rouge Metro area resulted in flash flooding.
episodes.201286: Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed across the Four State Region on March 28th in response to an upper-level disturbance moving across the Red River Valley of North Texas and Southern Oklahoma. As the afternoon hours progressed, strong southerly flow allowed for temperatures and dew points to rise, creating a more unstable atmosphere with MLCAPE values approaching 1000 J/kg. Thunderstorms started to strengthen in intensity during this period, with modest shear profiles across East Texas, Western Louisiana and adjacent Southwest Arkansas. Rotational signatures were detected in several of the stronger storms through the evening hours. This required the issuance of several tornado warnings across the aforementioned areas.  As a result, an EF0 tornado was reported in Caddo Parish. There was also some locally heavy rainfall with this event, with flash flooding being reported in Sabine Parish.
episodes.204211: Convective development along and north of the warm front with some pea to dime size hail in the Straits region early. During the evening hours, this convective activity was intensified by atmospheric gravity waves that allowed for strong downward momentum transport in an otherwise very stable low-level environment that was unfavorable for damaging winds. Scattered power outages prior to icing occurred with these storms, as well as some wind damage. Thunderstorms continued into the night, with precipitation across the M-68/M-32 corridors slowly transitioning from rain to freezing rain with time.
